public_rationale: The evidence points to concentrated infrastructure purchasing, but it does not establish the stated majority for the four named companies. The available estimate groups them with other providers and measures narrower asset purchases. Federal Reserve research also cautions that hyperscaler capex includes non-AI spending. Neither source settles the stronger claim of a massive US systemic weakness.
limitations: The target quarter is an interpretation of wording that mixes quarterly and annual figures.
The underlying IDC release could not be read; its figures are available through a specialist news report.
Concentration alone does not quantify systemic economic risk.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Most AI capex comes from big tech, which is a major systemic weakness in the US economy.

statement.excerpt: The reality is simple: the majority of all AI capex is from big tech, which is a massive systemic weakness in our economy.

from_speaker: the majority of all AI capex
a massive systemic weakness in our economy
our_interpretation: Big tech means Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet and Meta, the four companies identified in the surrounding discussion.
Majority means more than 50% of AI capital expenditure, measured consistently across the numerator and denominator.
The plain reading is that investment is concentrated enough that a spending retrenchment by these companies would materially threaten US economic activity.

For the ongoing observation, use April–June 2025, the latest completed reporting quarter before publication. The context mixes that quarter with full-year 2025 estimates; this is not treated as a forecast of completed full-year spending.
All AI capex has an unspecified geography. Test global spending first, while requiring US-specific evidence for the economic-risk clause.
The contextual comparison uses compiled spending estimates, so the accounting basis is estimate.
criteria.support_condition: Comparable estimates show the four companies supplying more than half of all AI capital expenditure during the target quarter, and credible analysis establishes material US economic exposure to that concentration.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Comparable estimates put their combined share at 50% or less, or credible analysis rejects the claimed material economic exposure. Evidence against only one component would not establish that every component is false.

evidence.locator: Paragraph beginning “By the way, in Q2”
evidence.explanation: The report attributes 86.7% of second-quarter AI infrastructure spending to hyperscalers, cloud builders and neoclouds. That broader group and its server-and-storage purchases do not establish the four named companies' share of all AI capex.

evidence.locator: Firm Investment and Adoption, discussion preceding Figure 4
evidence.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
evidence.explanation: The researchers identify an attribution problem with using hyperscaler capex as an AI investment measure. Their analysis does not provide the required target-quarter share or quantify systemic risk from the four companies.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A consistent target-quarter AI capex breakdown by company, plus analysis of the domestic output and financial exposure to a retrenchment by those companies.
